advances: For the complete lattice support of two positive horizontal resource rows over an arbitrary compact convex height domain in \(\mathbb R^k\), a convex potential and nonnegative concave budgets give an original curvature-cutoff score at least \(e^{-600}\widetilde W/((k+1)2^{n+k})\). When \(n\ge320(k+1)\), the factor \(k+1\) is removed. The proof obtains a symmetric lattice core from a parity-selected convex superlevel set, contracts it by an exact residue-difference injection, and uses the accepted horizontal reflection surplus on a common support. It then gives a point in an actual fiber for arbitrary convex-body fiber shapes whose volumes have the stated fixed-factor comparison. This proves the whole registered profile class; it asserts no representation of general convex bodies by this class.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The fixed-budget envelope, scaling, and horizontal reflection estimates are used through accepted fact `647ec0c586d3f2f8`, with their precise scope and aliases stated above. The scalar baseline and the point in the same actual fiber are used through accepted fact `03f071403cdfc69f`, with the two integer-dimension substitutions and all weight and score normalizations specified. The multivariate parity selection, convex symmetric core, integer contraction, original-curvature bound, and dimension-ratio estimate are proved here without a computer-certified finite premise.
proof:
Put \(\mathcal I:=Q\cap\mathbb Z^k\). This is finite and nonempty. Every height \(s\in\mathcal I\) contains the horizontal zero vector, because the budgets are nonnegative. For \(n\ge1\), every horizontal coordinate in \(P\) is bounded by \(\max_Q R/b_i\). The set \(P\) is closed by continuity, bounded, and convex by concavity of the budgets. Thus \(D\) is finite and nonempty and \(0<\widetilde W<\infty\). These conclusions also hold under the empty-horizontal convention.

The function \((x,t)\mapsto -V(t)-a\cdot x\) is concave on \(P\). Consequently the table \(\widetilde w\), extended by zero, satisfies the same-parity midpoint hypothesis of accepted fact `03f071403cdfc69f`. In applying that fact to this table, its integer dimension \(n\) is the present \(N\), its \(w,W\) are \(\widetilde w,\widetilde W\), and its \(j,v,\alpha(v),\mathcal U_j,\Delta_j(v),B_j^\Delta(L)\) are \(J,\xi,\widetilde\alpha_J(\xi),\widetilde{\mathcal U}_J,\widetilde\Delta_J(\xi),\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(L)\), respectively. In particular, the maxima in (1) are attained as in its finite-cutoff argument. Direct substitution gives the useful exact formula, for \(J=(j,s_0)\) and \(\xi=(v,u)\in\widetilde{\mathcal U}_J\),

\[
\widetilde\Delta_J(v,u)
=V(s_0+u)+V(s_0-u)-2V(s_0)\ge0.
\tag{5}
\]

The horizontal affine terms cancel; convexity of \(V\) proves the final inequality.

We use the fixed-budget assertions in the proof of accepted fact `647ec0c586d3f2f8`, with its horizontal \(n,a,b,c\) unchanged. Its fixed-budget support \(K_{\rho,\tau}\) is denoted \(\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\) here, its fixed-budget scalar table \(\widetilde w_z\) is denoted \(\omega_z^{\rho,\tau}\), and its reflection sum \(S_j^{\rho,\tau}\) is denoted \(\mathscr S_j^{\rho,\tau}\). Explicitly, for \(\rho,\tau\ge0\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}
&:=\{z\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n:b\cdot z\le\rho,\ c\cdot z\le\tau\},\\
\omega_z^{\rho,\tau}
&:=e^{-a\cdot z}\mathbf1_{\{z\in\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\}},\\
F(\rho,\tau)&:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\omega_z^{\rho,\tau},\\
\mathscr S_j^{\rho,\tau}
&:=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^n}
\min\{\omega_{j+v}^{\rho,\tau},\omega_{j-v}^{\rho,\tau}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The predecessor's \(F,\Psi,f,\beta,\gamma,\kappa_n,\eta_n\) retain their meanings. Namely, \(f(t):=\max_{m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}}\{\log(2m+1)-tm\}\) for \(t>0\), \(f(0):=+\infty\), and, when \(n\ge1\),

\[
\Psi(\rho,\tau):=\inf_{\beta,\gamma\ge0}
\left\{\beta\rho+\gamma\tau+
\sum_{i=1}^n f(a_i+\beta b_i+\gamma c_i)\right\}.
\]

For \(n=0\), let \(\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\) contain the empty vector and set \(F=1\), \(\Psi=0\). Put \(\kappa_n:=e^{-16\sqrt n-10}\) and \(\eta_n:=2n+2\log3\). Equation (2), its concavity assertion, and Equation (7) of that accepted proof give

\[
\begin{aligned}
F(\rho,\tau)&\le(3/2)^n e^{\Psi(\rho,\tau)},\\
\text{some }j\in\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\text{ satisfies}\quad
\mathscr S_j^{\rho,\tau}&\ge\kappa_n e^{\Psi(\rho,\tau)},\\
\Psi(t\rho,t\tau)&\le\Psi(\rho,\tau)+(t-1)\eta_n
\qquad(t\ge1),\\
\Psi((1-\varepsilon)\rho,(1-\varepsilon)\tau)
&\ge\Psi(\rho,\tau)-\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}\eta_n
\qquad(0<\varepsilon<1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]

Here \(\Psi\) is finite, nonnegative, concave, and nondecreasing in both budgets. These accepted assertions are quantified for all nonnegative fixed budgets and do not involve the predecessor's one-dimensional height domain or Gaussian potential. Its proof includes zero budgets: if \(n\ge1\) and either budget is zero, then \(\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}=\{0\}\), \(F=1\), \(\Psi=0\), and \(\mathscr S_0^{\rho,\tau}=1\). It also includes \(n=0\). Thus every use of (6) below has its full stated hypotheses.

For real \(t\in Q\), define \(\psi(t):=\Psi(R(t),T(t))\) and \(U(t):=\exp(-V(t)+\psi(t))\). Concavity of the budgets, followed by monotonicity and concavity of \(\Psi\), proves that \(\psi\) is concave on \(Q\). Hence \(\log U=-V+\psi\) is finite and concave there. Put \(U_s:=U(s)\) for \(s\in\mathcal I\), extend this table by zero outside \(\mathcal I\), and let \(Z:=\sum_{s\in\mathcal I}U_s\). These are the multivariate height quantities defined in the present proof. Since the original support contains every point of each permitted row, the first inequality of (6) gives

\[
\widetilde W
=\sum_{s\in\mathcal I}e^{-V(s)}F(R(s),T(s))
\le(3/2)^n Z.
\tag{7}
\]

The table \(U_s\) satisfies the same-parity midpoint hypothesis in height dimension \(k\). We give the precise parity-tail argument, which is the first scalar argument in `03f071403cdfc69f` with its dimension \(n=k\), table \(w=U\), and total \(W=Z\). For each nonempty parity class represented by \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}^k\), choose a maximizing height \(s_\sigma\in\mathcal I\cap(\sigma+2\mathbb Z^k)\), and put \(m_\sigma:=U_{s_\sigma}>0\). Convexity of \(Q\) and concavity of \(\log U\) show that

\[
\sum_{\substack{s\in\mathcal I\\s\equiv\sigma\pmod2}}
\sqrt{m_\sigma U_s}
\le
\sum_{\substack{s\in\mathcal I\\s\equiv\sigma\pmod2}}
U_{(s+s_\sigma)/2}
\le Z.
\tag{8}
\]

The midpoint map is injective for each fixed class, and all its images are integer heights in \(Q\). If \(0<U_s\le4^{-(k+1)}m_\sigma\), then \(\sqrt{m_\sigma U_s}\ge2^{k+1}U_s\). Thus the weight of these tail sites in one class is at most \(2^{-(k+1)}Z\). Summing over at most \(2^k\) classes leaves at least \(Z/2\) at the sites satisfying the strict inequality \(U_s>4^{-(k+1)}m_\sigma\) in their own class. No injectivity between different parity classes is asserted or needed.

Choose one class \(\sigma\) whose retained mass is at least \(Z/2^{k+1}\). Fix \(m_\sigma\) and set

\[
\zeta:=4^{-(k+1)}m_\sigma,\qquad
\mathcal E_\sigma:=\{s\in\mathcal I\cap(\sigma+2\mathbb Z^k):U_s\ge\zeta\},
\qquad E:=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal E_\sigma).
\]

The set \(\mathcal E_\sigma\) is finite and nonempty. The retained strict-superlevel sites lie in it, and every site of it has weight at most \(m_\sigma\). Therefore

\[
Z\le2^{k+1}m_\sigma|\mathcal E_\sigma|
=2^{3k+3}\zeta|\mathcal E_\sigma|.
\tag{9}
\]

Concavity of \(\log U\) gives \(U(t)\ge\zeta\) for every real \(t\in E\). Since \(E\subseteq Q\), this also proves the exact completeness relation \(E\cap(\sigma+2\mathbb Z^k)=\mathcal E_\sigma\). It does not require continuity of \(\Psi\) at a budget boundary.

We next obtain an integer center with a large symmetric core. Use the chart \(t=\sigma+2z\), and let \(\mathcal A:=((E-\sigma)/2)\cap\mathbb Z^k\). This is exactly \((\mathcal E_\sigma-\sigma)/2\). Every ordered pair \((h_1,h_2)\in\mathcal A^2\) in a common parity class has integer midpoint \((h_1+h_2)/2\in\mathcal A\), by convexity and the completeness relation. The map from such a pair to its midpoint \(h=(h_1+h_2)/2\) and displacement \(\upsilon=(h_1-h_2)/2\) is a bijection onto the pairs with \(h\in\mathcal A\) and \(h\pm\upsilon\in\mathcal A\). Thus Cauchy-Schwarz gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{h\in\mathcal A}
|\{\upsilon\in\mathbb Z^k:h+\upsilon,h-\upsilon\in\mathcal A\}|
&=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^k}
|\mathcal A\cap(\epsilon+2\mathbb Z^k)|^2\\
&\ge\frac{|\mathcal A|^2}{2^k}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]

Choose \(h\in\mathcal A\) whose summand is at least \(|\mathcal A|/2^k\), and put \(s_0:=\sigma+2h\in\mathcal E_\sigma\) and \(E_0:=(E-s_0)\cap(s_0-E)\). The compact convex set \(E_0\) is symmetric about zero and contains zero. Under the chart in (10), its points in \(2\mathbb Z^k\) are exactly the displacements \(2\upsilon\) counted at \(h\). Consequently

\[
|E_0\cap2\mathbb Z^k|\ge\frac{|\mathcal E_\sigma|}{2^k}.
\tag{11}
\]

Set \(q:=256\) and \(\delta:=2/q=1/128\). Partition the finite set \(E_0\cap2\mathbb Z^k\) by its \(q^k\) residue classes modulo \(2q\mathbb Z^k\). Choose a largest class and an anchor \(u_0\) in it. For each \(u\) in this class, \((u-u_0)/q\in2\mathbb Z^k\). Symmetry and convexity give \((u-u_0)/2\in E_0\), so \((u-u_0)/q\in\delta E_0\). This map is injective. In conjunction with (11), it proves

\[
|\delta E_0\cap\mathbb Z^k|
\ge\frac{|E_0\cap2\mathbb Z^k|}{q^k}
\ge\frac{|\mathcal E_\sigma|}{(2q)^k}.
\tag{12}
\]

No rank or interior condition was used in this argument. In particular, it applies to a singleton core. We will use all integer points of \(\delta E_0\), a symmetric set containing zero, rather than only the injected residue-class image.

For every real \(u\in\delta E_0\), the points \(s_0\pm u/\delta\) lie in \(E\subseteq Q\). Nonnegative concavity of \(R\) gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
R(s_0+u)
&\ge(1-\delta)R(s_0)+\delta R(s_0+u/\delta)
\ge(1-\delta)R(s_0),\\
R(s_0)
&\ge\frac1{1+\delta}R(s_0+u)
+\frac{\delta}{1+\delta}R(s_0-u/\delta)
\ge\frac1{1+\delta}R(s_0+u).
\end{aligned}
\]

The second line uses the exact convex-combination identity \(s_0=(s_0+u)/(1+\delta)+\delta(s_0-u/\delta)/(1+\delta)\). Applying these inequalities with \(-u\), and then applying the same argument to \(T\), proves

\[
\begin{aligned}
(1-\delta)R(s_0)&\le R(s_0\pm u)\le(1+\delta)R(s_0),\\
(1-\delta)T(s_0)&\le T(s_0\pm u)\le(1+\delta)T(s_0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]

This proves both directions even if either central budget is zero, without division by that budget.

Let \(\rho:=(1-\delta)R(s_0)\) and \(\tau:=(1-\delta)T(s_0)\). By (13), the complete horizontal support \(\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\) fits in every original row at height \(s_0+u\) with \(u\in\delta E_0\cap\mathbb Z^k\). Choose \(j\in\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\) from (6), and set \(J:=(j,s_0)\in D\). The scaling-down inequality in (6) yields

\[
\mathscr S_j^{\rho,\tau}
\ge\kappa_n\exp\left(\psi(s_0)-\frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\eta_n\right).
\tag{14}
\]

For every \(u\in\delta E_0\), the points \(s_0\pm u\) lie in \(E\), since \(0\in E_0\) and \(0<\delta<1\). In particular \(U(s_0\pm u)\ge\zeta\). Monotonicity of \(\Psi\), (13), and its scaling-up inequality give \(\psi(s_0\pm u)\le\psi(s_0)+\delta\eta_n\). Also \(U_{s_0}\le m_\sigma\) because \(s_0\) is in the selected parity class. It follows that

\[
\begin{aligned}
V(s_0\pm u)-V(s_0)
&=\psi(s_0\pm u)-\psi(s_0)
+\log U_{s_0}-\log U(s_0\pm u)\\
&\le\log(m_\sigma/\zeta)+\delta\eta_n
=2(k+1)\log2+\delta\eta_n,\\
e^{-V(s_0\pm u)}
&=U(s_0\pm u)e^{-\psi(s_0\pm u)}
\ge\zeta\exp(-\psi(s_0)-\delta\eta_n).
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]

Combining the first estimate with (5) bounds the curvature of every original pair centered at \(J\) with height displacement \(u\in\delta E_0\cap\mathbb Z^k\) by
\(\Theta_{n,k}=4(k+1)\log2+2\delta\eta_n\), exactly as defined in (2). This is a bound on the original potential's second difference.

For each such integer \(u\), and each \(v\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \(j\pm v\in\mathcal K_{\rho,\tau}\), the original endpoints \((j+v,s_0+u)\) and \((j-v,s_0-u)\) belong to \(D\). Their minimum original weight is at least
\(\zeta e^{-\psi(s_0)-\delta\eta_n}\min\{e^{-a\cdot(j+v)},e^{-a\cdot(j-v)}\}\), by (15). They all meet the original curvature cutoff. Distinct choices of \((v,u)\) are distinct oriented displacements. Both signs and zero are retained. Summing these contributions to the full original cutoff sum, and using (12) and (14), gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(\Theta_{n,k})
&\ge\frac{|\mathcal E_\sigma|}{(2q)^k}\,
\kappa_n\zeta\,
\exp\left(-\left(\delta+\frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\right)\eta_n\right)\\
&\ge\frac{|\mathcal E_\sigma|}{(2q)^k}\,
\kappa_n\zeta e^{-3\delta\eta_n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]

For the last inequality, \(\delta\le1/2\) implies \(\delta+\delta/(1-\delta)\le3\delta\). This summation uses no division by two. All pairs outside the chosen common support remain in the original score with their original weights.

Combine (7), (9), and (16), and multiply by \(2^N/\widetilde W\). Since \(N=n+k\), the result is

\[
\frac{2^N}{\widetilde W}
\frac{\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(\Theta_{n,k})}{1+\Theta_{n,k}}
\ge
\frac{(4/3)^n\exp(-16\sqrt n-10-3\delta\eta_n)}
{2^{3k+3}q^k(1+\Theta_{n,k})}.
\tag{17}
\]

Indeed, the factor \(2^k\) from \(2^N\) cancels the factor \(2^k\) in \((2q)^k\). Thus (17) keeps the normalization by the total mass of the complete support, including the tail discarded only in selecting the auxiliary core.

We bound the right side of (17) using elementary inequalities. First, \(\log(4/3)\ge1/4\), by integrating \(1/t\ge3/4\) from \(1\) to \(4/3\). Also \(\log2<1\) and \(\log3<2\). The identity \((\sqrt n-64)^2/8\ge0\) proves \(16\sqrt n\le n/8+512\). Since \(q=2^8\) and \(\delta=1/128\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
3\delta\eta_n&=\frac{3n}{64}+\frac{3\log3}{64}
\le\frac{3n}{64}+\frac3{32},\\
\log(1+\Theta_{n,k})&\le1+\Theta_{n,k}
\le4k+5+\frac n{32}+\frac1{16},\\
(3k+3)\log2+k\log q&=(11k+3)\log2\le11k+3.
\end{aligned}
\]

Consequently the logarithm of the right side of (17) is at least

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac n4-\frac n8-512-10
-\frac{3n}{64}-\frac3{32}
-(11k+3)-\left(4k+5+\frac n{32}+\frac1{16}\right)
&=\frac{3n}{64}-15k-530-\frac5{32}\\
&\ge\frac{3n}{64}-15k-531.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]

When \(n\ge320(k+1)\), this is at least \(-516\), and hence at least \(-600\). This proves (2) with the explicit original center and cutoff just constructed.

For the remaining range \(n<320(k+1)\), apply Equation (1) of `03f071403cdfc69f` to the original scalar table with the dimension and notation map already specified. It yields

\[
\max_{\substack{J\in D\\L\ge0}}
\frac{\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(L)}{1+L}
\ge\frac{\widetilde W}{24(N+1)2^N}
\ge\frac{\widetilde W}{7704(k+1)2^N}
\ge\frac{e^{-600}\widetilde W}{(k+1)2^N}.
\tag{19}
\]

Here \(N+1=n+k+1<321(k+1)\), and \(e^{600}>2^{13}=8192>7704\). Together with (2), this proves (1). The case \(n=0\) is included, because the accepted scalar dimension is \(N=k\ge1\). Every earlier core estimate also permits \(n=0\); no positive horizontal dimension, positive budget, or full-rank height lattice was used in its derivation.

Finally consider the actual body. Use the actual quantities \(\alpha_J(\xi):=\min\{w_{J+\xi},w_{J-\xi}\}\), \(\mathcal U_J:=\{\xi:\alpha_J(\xi)>0\}\), \(\Delta_J(\xi):=\log(w_J^2/(w_{J+\xi}w_{J-\xi}))\), and \(B_J^\Delta(L):=\sum_{\xi\in\mathcal U_J:\Delta_J(\xi)\le L}\alpha_J(\xi)\). Their meanings are exactly those of `03f071403cdfc69f` with its integer dimension \(n=N\), continuous dimension \(d\) unchanged, and \(j,v\) renamed \(J,\xi\). Its \(C,C_z,w_z,W,S,h_S\) are the actual objects of the present statement, and its \(\alpha(v),\mathcal U_j,\Delta_j(v),B_j^\Delta(L)\) are the actual quantities just defined. The scale \(\mathsf K\) in (3) is unrelated to that predecessor's scalar score \(K(w)\). In particular, the predecessor proves \(\Delta_J(\xi)\ge0\) for these actual volume tables.

The exact equality of positive supports gives \(\mathcal U_J=\widetilde{\mathcal U}_J\). For \(I\in D\), write \(w_I=\mathsf K\widetilde w_Ie^{\varepsilon_I}\), so that \(|\varepsilon_I|\le\log M\) by (3). For every displacement in the common pair support,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_J(\xi)&\ge\frac{\mathsf K}{M}\widetilde\alpha_J(\xi),\\
0\le\Delta_J(\xi)
&=\widetilde\Delta_J(\xi)
+2\varepsilon_J-\varepsilon_{J+\xi}-\varepsilon_{J-\xi}
\le\widetilde\Delta_J(\xi)+4\log M.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
\]

For any scalar center and cutoff \(J,L\), put \(L':=L+4\log M\). Since \(1+L'\le(1+L)(1+4\log M)\), (20) gives

\[
\frac{B_J^\Delta(L')}{1+L'}
\ge\frac{\mathsf K}{M(1+4\log M)}
\frac{\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(L)}{1+L}.
\tag{21}
\]

Choose \(J,L\) from (1), or choose the center in (2) and \(L=\Theta_{n,k}\) in the large-horizontal-dimension range. The upper comparison in (3), with zero volume outside \(D\), gives \(W\le\mathsf K M\widetilde W\). Thus (21) is at least \(e^{-600}W/[M^2(1+4\log M)(k+1)2^N]\), or at least \(e^{-600}W/[M^2(1+4\log M)2^N]\), respectively.

All hypotheses of Equation (3) of `03f071403cdfc69f` now hold at this same actual center: \(N,d\ge1\), \(C\) is a convex body, \(w_J>0\), \(W>0\), and \(L'\ge0\). That accepted conclusion supplies one \(y^\star\in C_J\) such that \(h_S((J,y^\star))\ge B_J^\Delta(L')/[12(1+L')]\). Substituting the preceding bounds proves (4) and its stronger version.

The center and cutoff are chosen before this point, and the point is chosen before every closed ambient halfspace. The accepted actual-fiber conclusion includes vertical halfspaces and boundaries containing entire fibers. Throughout the present proof, support inequalities, the definition of \(\mathcal E_\sigma\), and all curvature cutoffs use weak inequalities where specified. The strict tail selection only selects a subset for a lower bound and does not alter the original support. Empty and lower-dimensional integer fibers outside \(D\) remain part of \(S\) with zero contribution to its mixed volume. This establishes all stated quantifiers and boundary conventions.
statement:
Let \(k\ge1\) and \(n\ge0\) be integers, and put \(N:=n+k\). Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^k\) be a nonempty compact convex set with \(Q\cap\mathbb Z^k\ne\varnothing\). No full-dimensionality hypothesis on \(Q\) or its lattice support is imposed. Let \(R,T:Q\to[0,\infty)\) be finite continuous concave functions and let \(V:Q\to\mathbb R\) be a finite continuous convex function. For \(1\le i\le n\), fix \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i,c_i>0\). Define

\[
\begin{aligned}
P&:=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^k:
t\in Q,\ x_i\ge0,\ b\cdot x\le R(t),\ c\cdot x\le T(t)\},\\
D&:=P\cap\mathbb Z^N,\\
\widetilde w_{(x,s)}&:=\exp(-V(s)-a\cdot x)\quad((x,s)\in D),
\qquad \widetilde w_I:=0\quad(I\in\mathbb Z^N\setminus D),\\
\widetilde W&:=\sum_{I\in\mathbb Z^N}\widetilde w_I.
\end{aligned}
\]

For \(n=0\), use the unique empty horizontal vector, empty dot products equal to zero, and \(P=Q\). In all cases \(D\) is the complete support specified above; no lattice points are omitted. For \(J\in D\), set \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}_J:=\{\xi\in\mathbb Z^N:J+\xi,J-\xi\in D\}\), and define

\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde\alpha_J(\xi)&:=\min\{\widetilde w_{J+\xi},\widetilde w_{J-\xi}\},\\
\widetilde\Delta_J(\xi)&:=\log\frac{\widetilde w_J^2}
{\widetilde w_{J+\xi}\widetilde w_{J-\xi}}
\qquad(\xi\in\widetilde{\mathcal U}_J),\\
\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(L)&:=
\sum_{\substack{\xi\in\widetilde{\mathcal U}_J\\
\widetilde\Delta_J(\xi)\le L}}\widetilde\alpha_J(\xi)
\qquad(L\ge0).
\end{aligned}
\]

All logarithms are natural. Every displacement sum is oriented and includes zero. The curvatures are nonnegative, the score maximum below is attained, and

\[
\max_{\substack{J\in D\\L\ge0}}
\frac{\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(L)}{1+L}
\ge\frac{e^{-600}}{(k+1)2^N}\widetilde W.
\tag{1}
\]

If \(n\ge320(k+1)\), there is one \(J\in D\) for which

\[
\frac{\widetilde B_J^{\widetilde\Delta}(\Theta_{n,k})}{1+\Theta_{n,k}}
\ge e^{-600}2^{-N}\widetilde W,
\qquad
\Theta_{n,k}:=4(k+1)\log2+\frac{2n+2\log3}{64}.
\tag{2}
\]

For the actual-body consequence, let \(d\ge1\), let \(C\subset\mathbb R^N\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and put \(C_z:=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:(z,y)\in C\}\) and \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\). Empty and lower-dimensional fibers have zero volume. Suppose that the positive integer support is exactly \(\{I\in\mathbb Z^N:w_I>0\}=D\), and that, for some scale \(\mathsf K>0\) and comparison factor \(M\ge1\),

\[
\frac{\mathsf K}{M}\widetilde w_I\le w_I\le
\mathsf K M\widetilde w_I\qquad(I\in D).
\tag{3}
\]

Write \(S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^N\times\mathbb R^d)\), \(W:=\sum_{I\in\mathbb Z^N}w_I=\mathcal H_d(S)\), and \(h_S(p):=\inf_{H\ni p}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), over closed ambient halfspaces. Then there are \(J\in D\) and \(y^\star\in C_J\), selected before the halfspace, such that

\[
\begin{aligned}
h_S((J,y^\star))&\ge\frac{c(M)}{(k+1)2^N}W,\\
c(M)&:=\frac{e^{-600}}{12M^2(1+4\log M)}>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

When \(n\ge320(k+1)\), the center in (2) has a point in its same actual fiber satisfying the stronger bound \(h_S((J,y^\star))\ge c(M)2^{-N}W\). The coefficient in (4) depends only on \(M,k\), and the stronger coefficient depends only on \(M\). In particular, both are independent of \(n,d,V,Q,R,T,a,b,c,\mathsf K\) and the fiber shapes. All boundary equalities and all zero-volume integer fibers outside \(D\) are retained.
